children: German government bond yields were little changed on Monday following last week's rise, when strong US data stoked inflation concerns and brought expectations for three European Central Bank rate hikes by late 2027 back into market pricing.

Geopolitics stayed in focus, with Iran's army saying a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz while US President Donald Trump told advisers he may hold off on striking Iran if there are no new provocations from Tehran or the Houthis.
Germany’s 10-year government bond yields (DE10YT=RR) were flat at 3.11%. They hit 3.3895% on Friday, the highest level since October 22, and recorded their biggest weekly rise since mid-September.
German 2-year government bond yields (DE2YT=RR), more sensitive to expectations for policy rates, were down 0.5 basis points to 3.11%. They reached 3.1553% on Friday, the highest since October 14.

ECB euro short-term rate forwards implied the deposit rate would climb to 3.23% by late 2027 (EURESTECBM8X9=ICAP) from the current 2.50%, up from 3% priced in early this month. They also implied a rate of 2.75% by December.

The yield gap between French OATs and safe-haven German Bunds – a market gauge of the premium investors demand to hold French debt – was at 154 bps (DE10FR10=RR). It reached 177.71 bps on October 22, its highest level since mid-November 2011 at the height of the euro area’s sovereign debt crisis.
French OATs remained vulnerable ahead of next year's presidential election, with investors still fretting over France's fiscal trajectory.
